maya: quick Q — having a cross-language cursor + embeddings dim hiccup when piping pagination between clients

maya: workflow: Go service lists vectors and returns a base64 cursor, we feed that to a C# worker to continue a rerank. C# ends up parsing embeddings of length 1535 but server expected 1536. no intentional truncation steps.

samir: can you paste the exact error message and a redacted cursor payload?

maya: rerank error: "invalid_embedding_dim: expected 1536 got 1535"
maya: cursor (base64): `eyJwYWdlIjoxLCJvZmZzZXQiOjEwMCwiZW1iZWRkaW5ncyI6WzAuMTIzLDAuNDU2LC4uLDAuNzg5XX0=` — decodes to JSON but something off.

liam: two quick checks: 1) are you accidentally URL-encoding the cursor or using url-safe vs standard base64 across borders? 2) confirm both SDKs interpret bytes as UTF-8 and not trimming nulls. usually precision not count, but worth verifying.

maya: I tried Go: `base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString`, and C#: `Convert.FromBase64String`. Both produce a UTF-8 string.

maya: decoded preview: `{"page":1,"offset":100,"embeddings":[0.123,0.456,...,0.789]}`
maya: curious: Go reports raw.Length = 21456, C# reports raw.Length = 21455 immediately after decode.

samir: off-by-one in raw length — likely a dropped byte. Usual culprits: DB field truncation (varchar limit) or a buffer assembly bug in streaming code that drops last byte when chunk length % chunkSize == 0.

olivia: we had a similar customer report earlier this year. PR fixed trimming of trailing nulls in the Go SDK when using fixed-size buffers: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/4285 — check if that code path is shared.

liam: also grep both client libs for any manual Buffer.BlockCopy / Array.Copy with a `- 1` pattern in hot paths. We once had `Array.Copy(src, 0, dest, off, src.Length - 1)` that silently dropped the last byte when copying exact multiples.

maya: found a suspicious line in the C# StreamBuffer.Append: `Buffer.BlockCopy(chunk, 0, assembled, pos, chunk.Length - 1);` — whoops. opening a tiny PR to change to `chunk.Length`.

maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/5023 — fixes copy length, adds unit for boundary case where chunk boundaries align exactly with cursor length.

jo: will review in ~30m. when you open the PR, add an integration test that encodes a cursor with a trailing `}` and asserts decoded length equals original. also add a note in CHANGELOG and migration hint for persisted cursors in DB.

infra-bot: deploy bot: staging/redwood-sdk v2.19.1 rolled, CI green :white_check_mark:

samir: if PR merges, backport to C# v2.x branch and schedule a small DB migration script to re-encode affected cursors (or provide a token to re-run encode).

maya: will add a DB patch script and paste replication steps + test vector here. thanks for the rapid help.

samir: nice catch — this would have been a subtle production customer blip.

olivia: one more ask: if you can produce a minimal repro that swaps Go->C# and vice versa, drop into qa/soak for a day so we can be confident.

maya: yes — adding soak job and a test that cycles 10k cursor ops across both SDKs. will update this thread when jobs finish.

jo: reviewing PR now. ping me if you want a canary rollout on Dedicated infra.
